name: Methylmalonic Acidemia due to Cobalamin A Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for MMA cblA Defect

criteria.description: Elevated methylmalonic acid levels in plasma and/or urine
Reduced activity of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase enzyme in cultured fibroblasts or leukocytes
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the MMAB gene (cblA gene)
Presence of clinical features consistent with methylmalonic acidemia such as metabolic acidosis and neurological symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated methylmalonic acid plus either reduced enzyme activity or pathogenic MMAB gene mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is considered definitive; biochemical testing is essential for initial diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated methylmalonic acid
Recurrent episodes of vomiting and lethargy

laboratory: Markedly elevated methylmalonic acid in plasma and urine
Metabolic acidosis with increased anion gap
Elevated plasma homocysteine may be normal or mildly elevated
imaging: MRI brain showing basal ganglia abnormalities and cerebral atrophy
Renal ultrasound may show nephrocalcinosis or chronic changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MMAB gene confirming cblA defect
other: Reduced methylmalonyl-CoA mutase enzyme activity in fibroblasts or leukocytes

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in MMAB gene vs. MMACHC gene in cblB defect
Similar biochemical profile but different genetic cause
Elevated propionic acid rather than methylmalonic acid

redFlags: Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to standard treatment
Recurrent metabolic crises triggered by infection or fasting
references: Watkins D, Rosenblatt DS. Inherited disorders of cobalamin transport and metabolism. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2011.
Fenton WA, Gravel RA, Rosenblatt DS. Disorders of propionate and methylmalonate metabolism. In: Scriver CR et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. 2001.
